title: Sound
standard_text: Explore different actions to make sounds and how to make a variety of sounds, and recognise that sound energy causes objects to vibrate (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on sound: making sounds with instruments, vibrations, loud and soft sounds, and how sound travels to our ears. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Hitting, plucking, blowing and shaking make things vibrate. Bigger vibrations are louder.
body_html:
How to think about it

Sounds are made when things vibrate.

  • Hit a drum, pluck a string, blow a whistle.
  • Bigger vibrations make louder sounds.
  • Sound travels through the air to our ears.
Example

How does a guitar make a sound?

pluck the strings

they vibrate

Answer: vibrating strings

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sounds come from nowhere (something always vibrates).
  • Mixing up loud sounds with high sounds.

faq.a: A vibration is a very fast back-and-forth movement. You can feel it if you touch your throat when you hum.

faq.q: Why do sounds get quieter far away?
faq.a: The vibrations spread out as they travel, so less reaches your ears.

faq.q: How can children explore sound at home?
faq.a: Make a shaker with rice, a string telephone with cups, or tap bottles with different amounts of water.
